# Unicode search data

The shared source matcher embeds immutable tables derived from Unicode 17.0.0.
They implement locale-independent **simple** case folding (only C/S records)
and general-category lookup. No normalization, accent removal, full multi-scalar
folding or Turkic locale tailoring is applied. Whole Word uses L/M/N plus `_`.

| Official input | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| [CaseFolding.txt](https://www.unicode.org/Public/17.0.0/ucd/CaseFolding.txt) | `ff8d8fefbf123574205085d6714c36149eb946d717a0c585c27f0f4ef58c4183` |
| [UnicodeData.txt](https://www.unicode.org/Public/17.0.0/ucd/UnicodeData.txt) | `2e1efc1dcb59c575eedf5ccae60f95229f706ee6d031835247d843c11d96470c` |
| [UCD.zip](https://www.unicode.org/Public/17.0.0/ucd/UCD.zip), corresponding source | `2066d1909b2ea93916ce092da1c0ee4808ea3ef8407c94b4f14f5b7eb263d28e` |

`src/core/src/source_search_unicode_data.hpp` is generated by
`scripts/generate_source_search_unicode.py` from explicitly supplied input files,
then formatted with the repository's clang-format 22 script. The generator
refuses other digests and downloads nothing. Ordinary builds use the committed
header and acquire no Unicode dependency.

The complete [Unicode-3.0 notice](LICENSE.txt) was obtained from
[Unicode's license](https://www.unicode.org/license.txt) on 2026-10-13 and is
included in `package_runtime.NOTICE_FILES`. The release dependency inventory
binds the pinned UCD archive for SPDX and the separate corresponding-source asset.
This upkeep does not qualify or publish a release.
